contrasting2021Clubs.interpretation: The imported 2020 contract survivor gap is already large, but neither the balance nor its unexplained residual can be attributed to specific free-agent moves without the 2021 game transaction/payroll ledger.

limitations: 2021 screenshot amounts rounded; one team's $293K space is more precise than $329.7M committed.
A 2021 franchise has AI signings, releases, rookie deals and possibly dead cap not contained in the original V19 2020 snapshot.
Survivor salary+bonus is imported contract math, not verified actual 2021 charge per player; difference is unassigned rather than proved FA spend.
No salary, roster, development, rating, portrait, future draft, coaching or staff change is made by V28.

nextAction.candidateGuardrails: Any later separately versioned contract trial should explicitly model 2021 $330M, avoid initial 2020 over-cap, allow rookie signings, preserve V19 noncontract fields and all 4,320 draft prospects, and be validated in a separate new game.
nextAction.decision: Do not publish an unsafe V28 salary-adjusted Players file yet; the screen establishes the 2021 ceiling and team commitments but not which import salary/bonus/dead-cap fields contribute.
nextAction.evidenceNeeded: If available, expand Payroll's full cap panel for PIT/BAL to record base, bonus, dead money, full cap ceiling and player count; preserve current 2021 save.

relativeToV19Modeled2020Cap.qualification: The V19 $300M cap is an importer modeling assumption; this is not standalone proof of CapForge's 2020 game cap or a uniform yearly growth rule.

scope: PIT and BAL 2021 actual CapForge Payroll screenshots vs original unmodified V19 historical contracts and V27 2020/21 trade-market observations
